description: Local grounding knowledge for course inquiry classification and routing. Records are retrieved by keyword overlap and injected into the Laya decision request.

records.title: Add, drop, withdrawal, and waitlist policy
records.policy: Students add, drop, or withdraw from courses through the Registrar during the published add/drop or withdrawal window. Waitlists are automatic when a section is full, but a waitlist position does not guarantee enrollment. Enrollment and registration holds block registration until the office that placed the hold clears it.
records.review_note: Routine add/drop and waitlist questions can be answered from policy. Late adds or drops, deadline exceptions, overload requests, and hold disputes require registrar review.

records.title: Prerequisite checks and waiver approval
records.policy: Prerequisites are enforced at registration unless a waiver is approved. Waiver requests are reviewed by academic advising with the offering department, using prior coursework, placement results, or documented equivalent experience. Staff must not promise a waiver before a decision is recorded.
records.review_note: Prerequisite eligibility and waiver decisions require advisor or department review. Explain the process but do not confirm approval.
records.source: Academic Advising Service Description; Prerequisite Waiver Procedure

records.title: Section times, rooms, and schedule conflicts
records.policy: Official meeting times, rooms, and exam schedules are published in the timetable. Students should use the timetable for routine questions. Section changes, room conflicts, and schedule overrides are handled by the department or program administrator.
records.review_note: Routine timetable questions can be answered from the published schedule. Room conflicts, section changes, and exam overrides require department review.

records.title: Grade review and appeal process
records.policy: A student who believes a grade is incorrect should first contact the course instructor with the specific concern. If the issue is not resolved, the student may request review by the department according to the grade appeal procedure. Staff must not predict the outcome or quote appeal deadlines that are not in the current policy.
records.review_note: Grade appeals always require human review. Route to the instructor first and explain the department review step without judging the merits.

records.title: Incomplete grades and extensions
records.policy: An incomplete grade is granted only when the instructor approves a written plan for completing outstanding work. The student must meet the instructor's conditions and the deadline set in the plan. Support staff may explain the process but cannot grant an extension.
records.review_note: Incomplete grades and extensions require instructor approval. Do not promise an extension or change a deadline.

records.title: Syllabus, assignments, and course materials
records.policy: The course syllabus is the authoritative source for learning outcomes, assessment weights, assignment due dates, required textbooks, and course materials. Questions about content, readings, or assignment expectations should go to the course instructor.
records.review_note: Content and assignment questions route to the instructor. If the student cannot access materials, combine this record with the learning-platform support record.

records.title: Learning platform and portal access support
records.policy: Login, password, account, and platform-outage problems are handled by Student Support/IT Help Desk. Students should include their username, course, browser, error message, and time of the problem. Support staff never ask for a password. Once access is restored, missing assignment content is referred to the instructor.
records.review_note: Account, security, and outage issues require support review. Do not treat a login failure as a course-content or grading problem.

records.title: Instructor contact and office hours
records.policy: Instructor contact details and office hours are published on the course page and syllabus. Students should use the published university email or office hours. Staff must not share private contact information or personal schedules.
records.review_note: Routine contact questions can be answered from public course information. Route to the instructor when the student needs a response about the course.

records.title: Tuition, billing, payments, and refunds
records.policy: Tuition, fee, payment, balance, and refund questions are handled by Student Accounts through Student Support. Staff must not confirm whether a payment was received, promise a refund, or remove a financial hold based only on the inquiry text. The student should be referred with the term, student ID, and any receipt or transaction reference.
records.review_note: Financial account and refund decisions always require human review by Student Accounts.
records.source: University Fees and Refund Policy; Support Ticket Guidelines - Billing

records.title: Academic integrity and misconduct questions
records.policy: Academic integrity cases follow the university misconduct procedure. The course instructor or department handles the case; support staff must not determine whether misconduct occurred. Students should be directed to the instructor or the academic integrity office, and the inquiry should be escalated for human review.
records.review_note: Never judge guilt or innocence. Escalate academic integrity questions to the instructor or department.
